subject: gk
question: Which of the following correctly defines the difference between a major port and a minor port in India?

options.text: Major ports are under the Central government while minor ports are under the State government
Major ports are along the coasts, minor ports are on inland waterways
Major ports handle traffic within the country, minor ports handle exports
Major ports are publicly owned, minor ports are privately owned

solution:
The correct answer is __**Major ports are under the Central government while minor ports are under the State government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Major ports in India are governed by the Central Government through the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963.
 
• Minor ports are managed and controlled by the respective State Governments in India.
 
• There are 12 major ports in India, including Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata, among others.
 
• Minor ports are more numerous and include those like Pipavav in Gujarat and Krishnapatnam in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Major ports handle the majority of India's international maritime trade, whereas minor ports primarily cater to regional and local traffic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Port Trusts Act, 1963**

 
 
• This act provides the framework for the management and operation of major ports in India.
 
• It outlines the structure, function, and authority of port trusts that govern these ports.
 
• The Act also details the responsibilities of the Central Government in overseeing these ports.
 
 
 
• **State Maritime Boards**
 
 
• State Maritime Boards are responsible for the development and regulation of minor ports within their respective states.
 
• These boards work under the guidance of the State Government.
 
• They play a crucial role in facilitating coastal trade and smaller port operations.
 
 
 
• **Port Infrastructure**
 
 
• Major ports generally have more advanced infrastructure, including extensive cargo-handling facilities and deeper berths.
 
• Minor ports may have limited infrastructure but are vital for local trade and commerce.
 
 
 
• **National Maritime Development Programme (NMDP)**
 
 
• Launched by the Government of India to enhance port infrastructure and capacity.
 
• Aims to modernize both major and minor ports to meet the growing demands of trade.
